canonical_topic: Coal as a generation fuel: benefits and drawbacks
definition: Coal is a solid hydrocarbon fuel that is abundant, easy to store, and cheap to extract relative to the power it generates, but it is the most polluting fossil fuel, producing significant CO2 and SO2 emissions.
core_idea: Coal's low cost and logistical simplicity make it attractive for electricity generation, but its heavy carbon and sulfur emissions have made it increasingly unpopular and subject to competitive/regulatory pressure.
key_points: Coal is widely available globally and inexpensive to extract relative to its power output.
Easy to store compared to other fuels.
Major source of CO2 and SO2 emissions — its principal drawback.
Pollution concerns have driven declining consumer/public acceptance of coal generation.
relationships: Competing generation fuels (implied: natural gas, renewables)
